published_statement: Eq. (17), stated for the case 0 < beta < 1: 'the pressures at the throat are given by p_|| = -2 p_perp = -m/(4 pi beta r_0^3) = -beta^2/(32 pi m^2)', with throat radius r_0 = 2m/beta, from the metric ds^2 = A dr^2 + r^2 dOmega^2 - B dt^2, A = 1/(1 - 2m/(beta r)) (eq. 11), B = [1 + beta(sqrt(1 - 2m/(beta r)) - 1)]^2 / [same at r_obs]^2 (eq. 12), and the bulk pressures eq. (13) p_|| = -2 p_perp = (beta - 1) m / (4 pi beta [1 + beta(sqrt(1 - 2m/(beta r)) - 1)] r^3). Abstract: 'When the nonzero parameter beta lies in the open interval (0,1) one obtains traversable Lorentzian wormholes ... naked singularities when either beta < 0 or beta > 1 and the Schwarzschild black hole for beta = 1.' The paper does not print m_MS; m_MS = m/beta is the tree's (correct) reading of eq. (11).
published_hypotheses: static, spherically symmetric line element (4) in curvature coordinates, units c = G = 1
Einstein's equations of GR (7a-c), the geometry EXACTLY sourced by T (not a test field)
diagonal T: T^r_r = p_||, T^th_th = T^ph_ph = p_perp, T^t_t = -rho (eq. 6)
traceless T: rho = 0 AND p_|| + 2 p_perp = 0 (eq. 3) -- rho = 0 is imposed, not derived from T = 0
m > 0 implicit (m is 'the gravitational mass' fixed by the Newtonian limit, eq. 10); observer at infinity so B -> 1 - 2m/r
eq. (17) is stated for 0 < beta < 1 only; its cancellation (beta - 1)/(1 - beta) = -1 is invalid at beta = 1, where eq. (13) is identically 0
the region r >= r_0 = 2m/beta (no centre); the two-sided wormhole is built by eq. (19) with |sin psi|, i.e. a mirror gluing of two r >= r_0 patches

lacked_data: No empirical datum enters eq. (17): it is an exact solution of Einstein's equations under an imposed ansatz (rho = 0, p_|| + 2p_perp = 0), and the re-derivation reproduces every printed formula from the metric alone (58/58). So M's hypothesis -- that earlier physicists lacked some data -- has nothing to act on for the throat values: there is no measured input that a newer value could move. What the authors did NOT use, and could have (it was in print six months earlier, their own ref. [15]), is DKMV's global analysis: with it, the paper's global claim 'traversable wormhole for 0 < beta < 1' narrows to a smooth continuation for 0 < beta < 1/2, or to a mirror gluing with an unstated throat shell (sigma = 0, P = beta^2/(16 pi m (1-beta))). That is a completeness point about the paper's global construction, computed here, not a refutation of eq. (17), and it does not change the one-sided throat identity the tree uses. Evidence against M's hypothesis for this result: the tree's witness conclusion (traceless, static, spherically symmetric, rho = 0, p_|| < 0 at the throat with m_MS = m/beta > 0) is re-derived exactly.
grade_evidence: Eq. (17) itself STANDS: computed Einstein tensor of eqs. (11)-(12) reproduces eqs. (3), (13), (14), (17) exactly; r_0 = 2m/beta, 4 pi r_0^3 p_|| = -m_MS, m_MS = m/beta > 0, p_|| < 0 on all r >= r_0 for 0 < beta < 1; the tree's V19 = 0 and selftest row 8 agree. Nothing is WRONG. The grade is NARROWED because (1) the tree's alc_throat (tolman.py:1447-1454) drops the source's 0 < beta < 1 domain -- at beta = 1 the formula returns -1/(32 pi m^2) where the published solution has p = 0 (computed); (2) the tree's framing at tolman.py:254 and :531 ('each by removing exactly one hypothesis', 'removes nothing but tracelessness's sufficiency') is not true of this witness, which removes both the regular centre and the test-field background; (3) the source's global 'traversable wormhole for 0 < beta < 1' holds smoothly and shell-free only for 0 < beta < 1/2 (DKMV criterion, computed), and the tree's fixture beta = 1/2 sits on the boundary case, while ALC's own |sin psi| gluing carries an unstated thin shell. None of the three moves the tree's printed number or its conclusion 'tracelessness alone does not buy the biconditional', which holds on the one-sided r >= r_0 patch.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree's alc_throat guards 0 < beta < 1 (or the claim is stated for that range), tolman.py:254/:531 name ALC as removing the regular centre and the test-field background rather than one hypothesis, and 'wormhole' is qualified to the one-sided patch (or to 0 < beta < 1/2 / the mirror gluing with its shell). To WRONG: a computed error in eq. (13) or (17) -- none found in 58 checks. To OPEN: none; the source is read and the result is closed-form.
